title: Federal analysts detect anomalous Medicare billing, and $4.41 billion in claims is held in escrow
summary: Justice Department analysts detected anomalous Medicare billing through proactive data analytics, and $4.41 billion was held in escrow; no source names the software or says that it used AI.
account: In June 2024 the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services called the 2023 billing volume for two types of intermittent urinary catheter codes significant, anomalous and highly suspect. The American Hospital Association said that accountable care organizations had reported the suspect billing. On 18 June 2025 a federal indictment in the Eastern District of New York, United States v. Nakhmatullaev et al., set out the alleged scheme. On 30 June 2025 the Department of Justice reported that its analysts had detected the anomalous billing in Operation Gold Rush. The Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services held $4.41 billion in escrow from about $4.45 billion scheduled for payment. Medicare paid about $41 million, and supplemental insurers paid about $900 million. The Department of Justice stated that the health agencies intended to seek the return of the escrow to the Medicare trust fund. The announcement also proposed an AI-enabled Data Fusion Center. It does not establish that AI was used in the Gold Rush detection. On 3 February 2026 the Department of Justice announced that a Brooklyn banker had pleaded guilty to laundering proceeds of the Medicare fraud for the transnational criminal organization. It reported on 14 August 2026 that 35 people had been charged and 16 convicted, after a money-laundering guilty plea the previous day. These later announcements do not establish the final disposition of the $4.41 billion in escrow.
purpose: Detect, investigate and prosecute complex health care fraud schemes.
system: DOJ Health Care Fraud Unit proactive billing analytics
developer: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division Fraud Section, Health Care Fraud Unit Data Analytics Team
deployer: U.S. Department of Justice with HHS-OIG and CMS
domain: Health care fraud and public insurance

ratings.reason: The release states that $4.41 billion scheduled to be paid by Medicare was held in escrow for return to the Medicare trust fund. Supplemental insurers still paid about $900 million.
CMS and HHS-OIG stopped payment of all but about $41 million of $4.45 billion in claims from the organization, per the release.
The release describes over one million stolen identities but documents no outcome for the individual beneficiaries.

ai_role.statement: DOJ credits the detection to proactive data analytics by its Data Analytics Team and partners. It names artificial intelligence only for the Data Fusion Center that it announced in June 2025. The AHA reports that accountable care organizations also reported the suspect catheter billing, and CMS called the 2023 volume highly suspect in June 2024. No source says what methods flagged the claims or what share of the hold the analytics produced.
